acceptance.given: A historical wrapper replay claim is submitted with its recorded wrapper identity and launch evidence available.

oracle.expected: The validator accepts the replay only when execution evidence records that the original wrapper was actually launched, and rejects claims lacking that launch occurrence.
forbidden: Accepting a historical wrapper replay when no original wrapper launch occurred.
Treating indirect, inferred, or merely referenced execution as wrapper-launch evidence.
oracle.observable: A replay-validation result explicitly records wrapper-launch occurrence as a prerequisite and returns rejection for a no-launch historical replay claim.

acceptance.then: Run the historical replay validator against both a launch-backed record and an otherwise equivalent no-launch record; the launch-backed case is accepted and the no-launch case is rejected.
acceptance.when: When validating a historical wrapper replay.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the replay-validation test with historical evidence that omits any original wrapper launch; it must deterministically reject the claim.
Execute the replay-validation test with only indirect or inferred execution indicators and no recorded wrapper launch; it must reject rather than accept the historical replay.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce historical wrapper replay authorization by requiring literal evidence that the original wrapper was launched before accepting the replay claim; indirect or inferred execution cannot satisfy this prerequisite.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing historical replay records and command interfaces; rollback only the launch-occurrence enforcement while retaining append-only evidence and non-authorizing historical semantics.

slice_hint.state_transition: Historical replay validation transitions from pending claim to accepted only after original-wrapper launch occurrence is proven; otherwise it transitions to rejected.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A historical wrapper replay claim is accepted iff the validator observes recorded launch occurrence for the original wrapper; any no-launch, indirect, or inferred-only evidence yields rejection.

acceptance.given: The replay Matrix is assembled or verified from six Matrix Case records, each with distinct inputs and separated Stable and Candidate state, and the implementation must additionally bind a distinct fixture or state transition to every case.

oracle.expected: The matrix verification records six independently owned fixture or state-transition bindings, one for each Matrix Case, and rejects any case whose fixture or state-transition identity is reused by another case.
forbidden: A Matrix Case reuses another case's fixture or state transition.
Distinct labels or hashes alone establish case distinction.
oracle.observable: A runtime matrix-verification result contains six per-case fixture/state-transition ownership observations and reports rejection when any ownership identity is duplicated.

acceptance.then: When the replay Matrix is assembled or verified, execute the matrix ownership check and inspect its per-case ownership observations before accepting the result.
acceptance.when: The replay Matrix is assembled or verified.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the matrix ownership check against a controlled six-case matrix in which two Matrix Cases intentionally reference the same fixture or state-transition identity; the behavior test must produce an unsuccessful terminal result.

Run the matrix ownership check against six cases with distinct labels or hashes but no independently owned fixture or state-transition bindings; the verification must reject the matrix rather than infer ownership from labels or hashes.

affected_subjects: six replay Matrix Cases: valid package, invalid package, historical compatibility, dirty baseline, knowledge read-set collision, and closed-policy architecture-index gap
slice_hint.behavior_change: Extend matrix assembly and verification so each of the six Matrix Cases carries an independently owned fixture or state-transition binding in addition to distinct inputs and separated Stable/Candidate state; duplicate ownership and label/hash-only distinctions become unsuccessful results.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay receipt and Matrix Case schemas and terminal categories; reject only matrices lacking independent per-case fixture/state-transition ownership, without rewriting historical evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: Matrix assembly changes from recording case labels/inputs alone to recording and validating a unique fixture or state-transition identity for every case before aggregate evaluation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The matrix result is successful only if all six Matrix Cases execute with distinct inputs, separated Stable/Candidate state, and independently owned fixture or state-transition bindings; any duplicate binding, missing binding, or label/hash-only distinction yields an unsuccessful terminal result.

acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer is disabled through its repository real call surface with a captured Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

oracle.expected: The authored S7 selector executes disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through the real call surface; rollback restores the captured Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.
forbidden: CLI help, a schema file, a capability descriptor, or an old receipt is accepted as rollback evidence.
A simulated rollback is accepted in place of a real call-surface transition.
oracle.observable: Assertions in the S7 test observe the Consumer lifecycle transition and restored route, verdict, and diagnostic values.

acceptance.then: Each applicable Consumer has undergone behavioral rollback through its real call surface.
acceptance.when: The Consumer lifecycle is exercised by the authored S7 behavior test.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the S7 selector with a Consumer rollback implementation that bypasses the real call surface or fails to restore the captured baseline.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Author the S7 behavioral test and, if required, change skill_package_replay.py so every applicable Consumer performs disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through its real call surface while restoring its Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback must restore the captured Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline without changing the supported Consumer route contract.

slice_hint.state_transition: Disabled applicable Consumer -> real-call-surface behavioral rollback -> re-enabled Consumer with restored Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The exact S7 selector passes only after assertions observe real-call-surface rollback for every applicable Consumer and the restored captured baseline.

acceptance.given: An otherwise valid two-subject Matrix Case has a frozen expectation or expected output altered after its binding.

oracle.expected: The aggregate evaluator detects expectation-forged evidence and returns an unsuccessful aggregate verdict.
forbidden: Forged expected output or expectation is accepted.
The aggregate succeeds despite expectation-forged Matrix evidence.
oracle.observable: The aggregate result and case diagnostic identify expectation-forged evidence as the invalidating condition.

acceptance.then: Expectation-forged Matrix evidence cannot produce aggregate success.
acceptance.when: The matrix evaluator processes frozen expectations and expected outputs for both subject executions.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run an expectation-forgery fixture through matrix aggregate evaluation and require rejection instead of aggregate success.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make the Toolchain matrix aggregate evaluator reject a Matrix Case when its expected output or expectation differs from the frozen bound expectation identity; the forged evidence invalidates the aggregate.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Adds only fail-closed aggregate rejection for expectation-forged evidence; non-forged matrix evaluation and terminal failure categories remain compatible.

slice_hint.state_transition: Matrix evidence with an unauthenticated expectation transitions to an unsuccessful aggregate result when its forged expectation is detected.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: For an otherwise valid two-subject Matrix Case with an altered bound expectation, the aggregate is unsuccessful with an expectation-forged diagnostic and never succeeds.
